thread:
maria: Heads-up — we've started seeing dropped spans from our Python inference workers under high QPS. Likely exporter buffering overflow.

alex: repro logs? any pattern (model, seq len)?

maria: mostly p50 requests to large models. stack traces show the BatchSpanProcessor dropping spans when queue full. config is default OTEL processor.

jenn: are we using OTLP/gRPC or http/protobuf?

maria: OTLP/gRPC to our ingest gateway. exporter is the OTLP exporter shipped in our python sdk integration.

priya: hmm Python + GIL + high concurrency can cause spikes in the queue. we saw similar with metrics export during batched generation.

sam: For Go and Rust services, we had a pattern: tune BatchSpanProcessor: max_queue_size, max_export_batch_size, schedule_delay_millis. Also increased memory cap on the exporter.

alex: Question: should we centralize batching at the ingest gateway (single exporter) vs local batching in each worker? centralizing reduces duplicated buffers but adds network/availability coupling.

jenn: Centralizing sounds risky for Dedicated capacity where workers are isolated. + it would make per-tenant attribution harder unless we propagate resource/attributes.

priya: We need per-request attributes (model.name, model.variant, route:policy) on spans. If gateway batches from many workers, ensure attributes are attached before batching or we lose granularity.

maria: Another angle: adjust SDK init to use AlwaysOn sampler for critical request tracing, but sample 1% of token-level spans. Need consistent sampling across languages.

sam: Consistency across Python/Go/Rust is tricky: different sdk defaults, different semantic convention libs. We should standardize a small init helper: set_resource, set_sampler, install BatchSpanProcessor with our tuned params, and a resilient exporter with retry/backoff.

alex: Implementation note: Python SDK needs explicit flush on process exit — uvicorn uvloop workers can drop background threads. We should add an `atexit` flush + signal handler.

jenn: Rust async (tokio) tasks: make sure context propagation across spawn_blocking and tokio::spawn keeps the span. We've lost trace_id in a couple of places.

priya: Also watch attribute cardinality — model.id + prompt hash + user id will explode cardinality. Use hashed prompt_id, and only include model.name + quantization_profile.

maria: For exporter transport: OTLP/gRPC gives better throughput vs http/protobuf, but gRPC misconfig under load can stall. We should test both in load harness.

sam: Retention: our backend will sample/ingest high-volume spans for 7d and keep traces for 30d, but the ingestion cost skyrockets. Proposal: keep full traces for tail-sampled errors, aggregated metrics for normal ops.

alex: For SDKs, create language-specific examples: python snippet to init, go snippet with otel/sdk trace provider, rust snippet using opentelemetry + tonic exporter. Keep API shape similar.

maria: Example python init we could publish in our repo: ```python
from opentelemetry import trace
from opentelemetry.sdk.trace import TracerProvider
from opentelemetry.sdk.trace.export import BatchSpanProcessor
from opentelemetry.exporter.otlp.proto.grpc.trace_exporter import OTLPSpanExporter

provider = TracerProvider()
exporter = OTLPSpanExporter(endpoint="${OTEL_ENDPOINT}")
processor = BatchSpanProcessor(exporter, max_queue_size=2048, max_export_batch_size=512, schedule_delay_millis=1000)
provider.add_span_processor(processor)
trace.set_tracer_provider(provider)
```

jenn: That looks good. For Go: set MaxQueueSize and BatchTimeout accordingly. For Rust: the exporter builder has `with_batch_config`.

priya: Also add a local metrics counter for dropped_spans and expose it to Console so we can alert on >0.1% dropped over 5m.

alex: Agreed. Also tag spans with `routing.policy` and `dedicated_pool` when applicable so queries in Console can correlate latency with routing decisions.

maria: Final open item: durable buffering to disk for transient network partitions? It's complex but might be useful for on-prem Private deployments with flaky uplinks. Thoughts?

sam: Durable buffer would need careful cleanup and security (PII). I'd prefer retries + backpressure + circuit-breaker to avoid memory blowups.

jenn: For Private customers we could offer an opt-in local collector with persistent queue (like otel-collector with file_storage). That keeps SDKs simpler.

priya: OK next steps: 1) create cross-lang init helper + examples repo PR, 2) tune BatchSpanProcessor defaults (python 2048/512/1000), 3) add dropped_span metric & console alert, 4) run load tests OTLP gRPC vs http, 5) docs on attribute cardinality and sampling.

maria: I'll open the PR for python example and a test harness ticket. tagging y'all: @alex @jenn @priya @sam. :rocket:
